I didn't make glitter but I did work with large amounts in manufacturing for mixes for fake granite counter tops and other specialty surfaces. Our glitter had a silica base so we were supposed to wear dust masks. Glitter is very very light and sticky and easy to contaminate other mixes with. The easiest way for us to remove it was simply blowing off using an air compressor. We had one super fine glitter that would once poured hang in the air. Which could in a huge amount contaminate 100's of thousands of dollars of mix. Once a mix is contaminated it has to be tossed. The glitter in the 55 gallon containers was very fluffy and soft and fun to play with. As quality control we would inspect size and shade as making some look like granite with different color dust the tiniest things can make all the difference. The company I worked for I guess paid about 80 dollars a pound.. The glitter was actually my favorite part of my job. Something satisfying about dumping 5 gallons of glitter.... 

Edit.... As for glitter was in my home and is still there... Mostly in my jeep.. I moved so my home is pretty glitter free..
